subject: geography
title: UK Regeneration Cases
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on UK regeneration, gentrification and Liverpool/Salford cases.

concepts.def: Long-term comprehensive improvement; economic, social, environmental.
Reshaping place image to attract investment or visitors.
Wealthier residents replacing original community; rents rise.
Iconic build to spark wider change; Tate Liverpool.
University expansion changing demographics (e.g. Selly Oak).
Movement to rural areas; common in MEDC; Norfolk, Devon.

walkthroughs.body_html: Albert Dock derelict by 1981 Toxteth riots; Tate Liverpool opened 1988. Capital of Culture 2008 attracted £750 million investment, 9.7 million extra visitors. Lost UNESCO status 2021 over Liverpool Waters development. Population still below 1930s peak but growing.

Manchester Ship Canal redundant by 1980; redevelopment from 1985. Lowry Centre 2000; Imperial War Museum North 2002; MediaCity UK 2007 (BBC + ITV, 4400+ jobs). Local employment rates rose. Some original residents feel disconnected from new opportunities.

Shoreditch transformed since 2000: house prices rose from £150000 to £900000+. Original Bengali community displaced. Coventry Climax site in Heygate redeveloped Elephant & Castle: 1200 social homes demolished, 82 social replacements. Regeneration creates winners and losers.
